observation_summary: The application throws an OutOfMemoryError when processing a large number of observations because it attempts to instantiate a full N x N matrix for weights, even when the weights are uncorrelated (diagonal).
hypothesis: The squareRoot method in AbstractLeastSquaresOptimizer performs an expensive EigenDecomposition on the weight matrix regardless of its structure. For diagonal weight matrices, this is computationally inefficient and memory-intensive, leading to heap exhaustion.
prediction: The fix will introduce a check to detect if the weight matrix is an instance of DiagonalMatrix and, if so, compute the square root by taking the square root of the diagonal elements directly, avoiding the full matrix decomposition.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the addition of an 'if (m instanceof DiagonalMatrix)' block that implements a specialized, memory-efficient square root calculation for diagonal matrices, confirming that the original algorithm was suboptimal for this common case.
reasoning_summary: The defect is an efficiency and correctness problem in the computational procedure (squareRoot). The original implementation used a generic, memory-heavy algorithm (EigenDecomposition) for all matrices. The fix introduces a specialized, more efficient algorithmic path for diagonal matrices, which is a classic 'Algorithm/Method' correction.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a check (instanceof), the primary purpose is to switch to a more efficient computational algorithm, not to validate input parameters or prevent invalid states.
The fix does not require a design-level capability change; it optimizes an existing internal procedure to handle large data sets correctly.
